## Pre-flight checklist

### One week before

1. Check the date and the room in the [KSL course entry](https://www.ksl.unibe.ch/KSL/kurzansicht?stammNr=526141&semester=HS2026&lfdNr=0).
2. Check the enrolment list. The instructor expects mostly DH Major students; prepare the Minor and elective caveat ([U-03](../project-management/risks.md)).
3. Send the [Setup](setup.qmd) page to the participants. Ask the command-line learners to complete [Prepare the command line](setup.qmd#command-line-route) before the session.

### The day before

1. Run X1 to X6 in a fresh test account or a fresh repository. Compare each step with the [UI verification log](#ui-log). Check X5 and X6 too: they are optional, but learners use them in the consolidation block and after the session.
2. Run the **Command line** tabs of X1 to X6 in a private throwaway repository. Compare each step with the [command-line verification log](#cli-log). Delete the repository and the Project afterwards.
3. Update a screenshot if the interface changed. Run `npm run screenshots:annotate`.
4. Check that the [showcase Project](https://github.com/users/maehr/projects/11) is public and linked to the course repository.
5. Check [githubstatus.com](https://www.githubstatus.com/).

### On the day

1. Open the [slides](../slides/index.qmd), the showcase Project, and the example repository in separate tabs.
2. Write the Wi-Fi details and the site URL on the board.

## Timing

X1–X4 form the core workshop. X5 and X6 are optional, self-paced extensions; they have no block in the run of show ([D-014](../project-management/decisions.md#d-014)). Teach the essential actions of each core exercise; skip a step that starts with **Optional:** when the group runs late.

| Block | Planned | Risk | Cut if late |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Frame | 15 min | Discussion runs long | Show the comparison table of the [approaches](approaches.qmd) only; skip the discussion |
| X1 | 30 min | Account creation, two-factor authentication | Pair learners without an account; skip **Optional: stop the template workflows** |
| X2 | 40 min | Deriving E01-T1 takes long | Give five minutes for E01-T1, then compare with the backlog; skip **Optional: check one rule and one story** |
| X3 | 45 min | Linking, visibility, and dates take time | Skip **Optional: check the workflows**, the second dependency, and the M2 justification |
| X4 | 40 min | Merge conflicts, review rights | Self-review with **Comment** |
| Consolidate and extend | 35 min | Learners are at different stages | See [the consolidation block](#consolidate) |
| Transfer and closing reflection | 15 min | — | Reflection in pairs |

### The consolidation block {#consolidate}

The block from 12:10 to 12:45 is not an exercise. It gives every learner time to reach a working core workflow.

1. Ask the group which step of X1–X4 is still open. Solve a common problem once, for the whole group.
2. Help the learners whose workflow is incomplete first. The [solutions](solutions.qmd) show the expected state of each exercise.
3. Learners whose workflow is complete start an optional extension: [X5](exercises/x5.qmd) for publication, [X6](exercises/x6.qmd) for re-planning. Neither extension needs the other.
4. Stop at 12:45, also when learners are in the middle of an extension. They can continue after the session.

### Closing reflection

The closing reflection is informal. It does not test anything, and it does not affect the pass rule. Use the [three questions](syllabus.qmd#closing-reflection) in pairs or in the group. Then show [After the workshop](after.qmd).

## Known failure modes

| Symptom | Cause | Response |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Red cross and e-mails after X1 | The template workflows run on the first commit and fail at the Pages deployment (404) and the link check | Expected. Show **Settings → Actions → General → Disable actions**. |
| Copilot fills in commit messages and requests reviews | Account settings of the learner | Use it as an example: read and replace AI text. A Copilot review can fail with a quota message. |
| Workflows show error icons | Status options renamed after the Project was created | Edit the workflows and select an existing option. |
| Roadmap settings lost | The confirmation dialog after **Save view** was not confirmed | Repeat and confirm with **Save**. |
| `CITATION.cff` shows the template | The template ships its own citation file | X5 corrects it. |
| A learner commits real data | — | Stop, remove the file, and explain that the history keeps it. For real data, the repository must be deleted or cleaned. Prevention: synthetic data only. |

## Teaching points

- **Rules versus plans.** KSL governs this course, not the thesis. Thesis rules come from the study plan and the faculty regulations, and they differ per programme.
- **Hierarchy versus dependency.** Parent-child means "part of"; blocked-by means "waits for".
- **Milestone versus date field.** A milestone groups work under a due date in the repository; date fields schedule each item in the Project.
- **Release versus deposit.** A GitHub release is not preservation. A DOI comes from a repository such as Zenodo, and only after an explicit decision.
- **What GitHub cannot guarantee:** quality, deadline compliance, confidentiality, and long-term preservation.

## Command-line verification log {#cli-log}

The instructor ran every **Command line** tab of X1 to X6 on **13 October 2026** in zsh on macOS, with gh 2.102.0 and git 2.54.0. The run used a private throwaway repository and a private copy of the showcase Project. A second run on the same day, with the same versions, tested the commands that changed after the review of pull request #16. It created the Issues in another order than X2: an extra Issue first, then E08, then E01. Windows and Git Bash were not tested.

| Exercise | Command | Observation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| X1 | `gh repo create … --template … --clone` | The clone contains the template files at once. |
| X1 | `gh api -X PUT …/actions/permissions -F enabled=false` | The read-back showed `true` for a few seconds, then `false`. |
| X2 | `gh issue view … --json body --jq .body \| gh issue create … --body-file -` | The bodies of the example Issues are identical to `backlog.yml`. In a new repository, E01 is #1 and E08 is #2. |
| X2 | `gh issue create --parent` | `gh issue view` lists the sub-issues and their progress. |
| X3 | `gh api …/milestones -f due_on=…` | On creation, `T00:00:00Z` stored the day before, for example 2027-05-31 for 2027-06-01. `T12:00:00Z` stored the right day. A change with `-X PATCH` stored the right day with both times. |
| X3 | Helper `issue`, with the Issues in another order | Each lookup returned the right number, also for an Issue created one command before. A partial ID such as `E0` returned nothing. |
| X3 | `gh project copy` | In a terminal, gh prints the address of the copy. The copy starts private. |
| X3 | `gh project link N` with `--owner @me` | Failed in three forms. With `--repo NAME` and without `--repo`: "Could not resolve to a Repository with the name '@me/…'". With `--repo OWNER/NAME`: "has different owner from '@me'". `gh project link N` without flags, in the folder of the repository, worked. |
| X3 | `gh issue edit … --add-project` for the two epics | With both epics in one command, the second failed with "created a temporary conflict". One Issue per command worked. The workflow added the six sub-issues with Status Backlog after about 70 seconds. In the first run, `gh project item-add` took less than ten seconds. |
| X3 | `gh issue edit --add-blocked-by` | `gh issue view` shows the line `blocked-by`. |
| X4 | `gh issue develop --name … --checkout`, `gh pr create` | The Status changed to In review. In the second run, it still showed Backlog after 6 seconds and In review after 18 seconds. |
| X4 | `gh pr merge --merge --delete-branch` | gh switched the folder to `main` and pulled. The Issue closed as completed, and the Status changed to Done. |
| X5 | `gh api …/contents/… -H "Accept: application/vnd.github.raw"`, `git add` | The file has the same content as the CSV of the course repository. git warns that LF will be replaced by CRLF, because the template sets this line ending for CSV files. |
| X5 | `git commit -m … -m "Closes #7"` on `main` | The push closed the Issue as completed. |
| X5 | `gh release create`, `gh issue close --comment` | Release and closed Issue as expected. In the second run, `gh release view --json url` put the address of the release into the comment. |
| X6 | `gh issue create --parent … --milestone … --blocked-by …` | One command sets the parent, the milestone, and the dependency. The workflow added the new sub-issues to the Project. |
| X6 | `gh api -X PATCH …/milestones/2` | The due date of M2 changed and changed back. |
| X6 | `gh project item-list --format json` | The file lists every item with its Status. A field without a value is not in the file. gh does not apply the filter of a view. |
| All | Project fields, workflows, access, status update | No gh command, or a command that needs internal IDs (field values). The exercises mark these steps **Browser only**. |
